hunks.baseline: What made humans seem so special in a world teeming with countless living things was their ability to think deeply and broadly.
hunks.sol: What made humans seem so special in a world teeming with life was their ability to think deeply and broadly.

hunks.baseline: That was true of every human being.
hunks.sol: Every human could do it.

hunks.baseline: They took in their current situation through their eyes and ears, thought about what to do or say to the person in front of them, and put together the right words.
hunks.sol: They took in a situation with their eyes and ears, considered what to do or say to the person in front of them, and chose their words.

hunks.baseline: At the same time, they predicted what would happen because of their words and actions.
hunks.sol: At the same time, they predicted what those words and actions would bring about.

hunks.baseline: But those predictions didn’t always come true.
hunks.sol: But their predictions weren’t always right.

hunks.baseline: When the situation around them took an unexpected turn, or the person they were talking to reacted in a way they hadn’t anticipated, humans were thrown off.
hunks.sol: When things took an unexpected turn, or the person they were talking to reacted in a way they hadn’t anticipated, they were thrown off.

hunks.baseline: Their minds, spinning at full speed, came to a halt. They lost all sense of what to say.
hunks.sol: Their racing thoughts came to a halt. They lost their words.

hunks.baseline: Just like I was right now.
hunks.sol: Just like me, right now.

hunks.baseline: So Gyo—no, the Bow Saint—stared at me. Her lips moved, and a voice only I could hear slipped between them.
hunks.sol: So Gyo—no, the Bow Saint—studied me. Her lips moved, and a voice only I could hear slipped between them.

hunks.baseline: The shock of learning that So Gyo was the giant known as the Bow Saint had completely disappeared.
hunks.sol: The shock of learning that So Gyo was the legendary figure known as the Bow Saint vanished without a trace.

hunks.baseline: Those few words, transmitted like a hammer blow to the back of my head, left me blinking blankly.
hunks.sol: That brief Sound Transmission hit me like a sledgehammer to the back of the head. I could only blink.

hunks.baseline: I thought she’d explain that she hadn’t expected things to turn out this way, that she’d had no choice—especially since I wasn’t hiding my anger.
hunks.sol: With me making no effort to hide my anger, I thought she’d say she hadn’t expected things to turn out this way. That she’d had no choice.

hunks.baseline: As I froze like a statue at that utterly unexpected combination of words and their incomprehensible meaning, the Bow Saint’s Sound Transmission continued.
hunks.sol: I stood frozen like a statue, unable to make sense of those words or what they meant. Then the Bow Saint’s Sound Transmission continued.

hunks.baseline: But the question that flashed through my mind was cut short before it could even take shape.
hunks.sol: But I had to set those questions aside almost as soon as they occurred to me.

hunks.baseline: *—It’s a long story I’ve kept to myself. But this isn’t the best place to talk.*
hunks.sol: *—It’s a long story I’ve kept to myself. But talking here and now wouldn’t be wise.*

hunks.baseline: I desperately wanted to press her for answers, but the Bow Saint’s Sound Transmission was enough to remind me of the situation I’d momentarily forgotten.
hunks.sol: I wanted nothing more than to press her for answers, but her words reminded me of the situation I’d momentarily forgotten.

hunks.baseline: The massive bloodbath that had unfolded here today was over, but that didn’t mean everything was finished.
hunks.sol: The bloodbath that had unfolded here today was over, but not everything was finished.

hunks.baseline: Just as a curtain call still follows when the curtain falls on a performance.
hunks.sol: The curtain had fallen, but the curtain call remained.

hunks.baseline: I nodded. The Bow Saint understood what I meant and quietly turned away.

hunks.baseline: Her gaze flicked toward the one person who’d stood beside us all along, watching everything in silence.
hunks.sol: I nodded. The Bow Saint understood and quietly turned away, flicking a glance at the one person who’d stood beside us all along, watching in silence.

hunks.baseline: “That old hag’s still the same. No, she’s even more irritating now that she’s gotten younger. Her eyes are worse than before.”
hunks.sol: “That old hag hasn’t changed. No, she looks younger, but the look in her eyes is even more unpleasant.”

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang muttered it under his breath, then added, “And playing games with some young punk through Sound Transmission right in front of me, too.”
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang muttered under his breath, then added, “Playing games through Sound Transmission with some young punk right in front of this old man, too.”

hunks.baseline: I peeled a crust of dried blood off my cheek and answered, “I figured you’d know. And even if you didn’t, I would’ve told you myself.”
hunks.sol: I peeled a crust of dried blood off my cheek. “I figured you would. And even if you hadn’t, I would’ve told you myself.”

hunks.baseline: “Then I’ll tell you. Every last word. I won’t leave out a single syllable.”
hunks.sol: “Then I’ll tell you. Every last word.”

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang stared at me for a moment, then clicked his tongue.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang studied me for a moment, then clicked his tongue.

hunks.baseline: “Forget it. There’s no rush. She must have had her reasons. Anyway…”
hunks.sol: “Forget it. There’s no rush, and she must have had her reasons. Anyway…”

hunks.baseline: His sturdy palm tapped my shoulder. Jeok Cheongang quickly turned his head away, and his gruff voice came from his profile.
hunks.sol: His solid palm tapped my shoulder. He turned his head sharply away, speaking in a gruff voice.

hunks.baseline: “Uh, well. What I’m trying to say is… hmm.”
hunks.sol: “Well, uh…”

hunks.baseline: “No, I mean. What this old man wants to say is… Hey, look at you. Are you laughing?”
hunks.sol: “No, what this old man means to say is… Hey, look at you. Are you laughing?”

hunks.baseline: At some point, a laugh must have slipped out of me.
hunks.sol: A laugh must have slipped out without my realizing it.

hunks.baseline: But I didn’t hurriedly wipe the smile from my lips like I used to.
hunks.sol: But I didn’t rush to wipe the smile from my face like I used to.

hunks.baseline: I knew how he felt. And he’d understand what I was feeling, too.
hunks.sol: I knew how he felt. And he’d understand how I felt, too.

hunks.baseline: *Thank you. For coming back to me.*
hunks.sol: *Thank you. For coming back.*

hunks.baseline: That was what Jeok Cheongang had said just a little while ago, when I’d been hovering between life and death, after I finally clawed my way back from death and recovered.
hunks.sol: That was what Jeok Cheongang had said when I’d returned from the brink of death just a little while ago.

hunks.baseline: And now it was my turn to say it back to him.
hunks.sol: Now it was my turn to say it to him.

hunks.baseline: “Thank you. For always staying by my side.”
hunks.sol: “Thank you. For always being by my side.”

hunks.baseline: I murmured so quietly he could barely hear, then pretended to be distracted by something in the air.
hunks.sol: I murmured it barely loud enough to hear, then looked up at the empty air as if something there had caught my attention.

hunks.baseline: It was a little embarrassing. And I wasn’t sure I could handle seeing his reaction.
hunks.sol: It was a little embarrassing, and I wasn’t sure I could face his reaction.

hunks.baseline: But… well. Sometimes you just want to say something like that.
hunks.sol: But… well. Sometimes you want to say these things.

hunks.baseline: Even when you’re close enough that you don’t need long explanations, there are times when you simply want to speak from the heart.
hunks.sol: Even when you know each other so well that long explanations aren’t needed, sometimes you just want to tell someone how you feel.

hunks.baseline: And in that regard, at least, Jeok Cheongang was far clumsier than his immense martial prowess would suggest.
hunks.sol: And for all his immense martial prowess, Jeok Cheongang was remarkably bad at that.

hunks.baseline: “Ahem. Ahem. What’s with that creepy stuff coming from a hairy bastard like you…”
hunks.sol: “Ahem. What’s a hairy bastard like you doing saying something so revolting…”

hunks.baseline: He hesitated, clearing his throat for no good reason, then suddenly gave a quiet laugh. At the end of the direction his finger pointed, a group of people was rushing closer.
hunks.sol: He hesitated behind another unnecessary cough, then let out a quiet laugh. In the direction he pointed, a group was hurrying toward us.

hunks.baseline: “This old man’s a given. Save your thanks for those guys. They threw themselves into a deathtrap just to save you. They deserve at least that much praise, don’t they?”
hunks.sol: “This old man’s a given. Save your thanks for them. They threw themselves into a deathtrap just to save you. They deserve at least that much praise, don’t they?”

hunks.baseline: I turned my head. Familiar faces came into view, hurrying toward me with blood covering them from head to toe.
hunks.sol: I turned. Familiar faces were rushing toward me, drenched in blood from head to toe.

hunks.baseline: Every one of them had survived. Not a single person was missing.
hunks.sol: They’d all survived. Not one of them was missing.

hunks.baseline: Was it the overwhelming relief? Or the exhaustion I’d forgotten about?
hunks.sol: Was it the overwhelming relief? Or the exhaustion I’d forgotten?

hunks.baseline: In an instant, all strength left my body. I staggered and began to fall.
hunks.sol: All the strength went out of me at once. I staggered and began to fall.

hunks.baseline: If a flurry of hands hadn’t reached out from every side to catch me, I certainly would have.
hunks.sol: Hands reached out from every side and caught me before I could.

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang, Hyuk Mujin, Ju Hwaran, Song Ilseom, Sama Pyo, Taishan, and the Divine Physician caught my arms and legs. They held up my body as it threatened to tip over.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang, Hyuk Mujin, Ju Hwaran, Song Ilseom, Sama Pyo, Taishan, and the Divine Physician caught my arms and legs. They held me up as I started to topple.

hunks.baseline: Not like a heavy burden, but like sturdy pillars.
hunks.sol: They weren’t a burden to bear. They were pillars holding me steady.

hunks.baseline: Every one of them had come back to this deathtrap, hoping they could help even a little. Each of them had become the greatest reason I had to win this horrific battle.
hunks.sol: Each of them had returned to this deathtrap hoping to help, even a little. Each had become my greatest reason to win this horrific battle.

hunks.baseline: “Damn it. I should be lending a hand in this awesome moment, but this guy’s so tall I can’t even reach him.”
hunks.sol: “Damn it. I should be lending a hand at a moment like this, but this guy’s so tall I can’t reach him.”

hunks.baseline: At the mournful remark from the old Hidden Shadow Pavilion agent perched on Taishan’s shoulder, everyone let out a quiet laugh.
hunks.sol: At the mournful complaint from the old Hidden Shadow Pavilion agent perched on Taishan’s shoulder, everyone let out a quiet laugh.

hunks.baseline: Even I, who’d nearly closed my eyes against the sleep demon washing over me.
hunks.sol: Even me, though I’d been about to close my eyes and give in to the sleep demon.

hunks.baseline: I clenched my teeth and forced strength back into my crumbling body. Then, ignoring the worried looks around me, I started walking.
hunks.sol: I clenched my teeth and forced strength back into my failing body. Then I left their worried looks behind and started walking.

hunks.baseline: *Clop. Clop.*
hunks.sol: *Step. Step.*

hunks.baseline: Past the dead and the rebels, bound tight in thick iron chains and struggling to break free.
hunks.sol: Past the undead and the rebels, bound tight in heavy iron chains and struggling to break free.

hunks.baseline: Looking toward the dozens of flags rising high into the air.
hunks.sol: Past dozens of flags rising high above me.

hunks.baseline: Until, at last, in that vast space where not a single protest or scream could be heard, I saw the monster writhing alone at the Bow Saint’s feet.
hunks.sol: Until, at last, I saw the monster writhing alone at the Bow Saint’s feet. Across that vast space, there were no more cries of protest or screams.

hunks.baseline: At my call, the monster’s movements stopped abruptly.
hunks.sol: At my call, the monster stopped moving.

hunks.baseline: This hollow sense of defeat and fury, now that he could no longer achieve his goal.
hunks.sol: To put an end to the emptiness and fury of knowing he could no longer achieve his goal.

hunks.baseline: A volcano that had spewed lava soon cooled. The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord was the same now.
hunks.sol: A volcano cooled soon after spewing its lava. Now the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord had cooled, too.

hunks.baseline: “Well, I don’t think that applies to an immortal monster like you.”
hunks.sol: “Well, I don’t think that applies to a monster like you who can’t even die.”

hunks.baseline: “A monster, is it? So that’s how it is?”
hunks.sol: “A monster, is it? So that’s how you see me?”

hunks.baseline: “Right. And to be precise, I’m not exactly big on manners even with people.”
hunks.sol: “Yeah. And to be precise, I’m not exactly polite to people, either.”

hunks.baseline: “Didn’t you just call me a monster who wouldn’t die?”
hunks.sol: “Didn’t you just say I couldn’t die?”

hunks.baseline: “I think I know what you mean. That makes sense.”
hunks.sol: “I think I know what you mean. You have a point.”

hunks.baseline: Even after all these long years, the pain of it still lingered faintly.
hunks.sol: Even after all these years, he could faintly remember how it had hurt.

hunks.baseline: “Yes, I remember. I had times like that, too. My Master was usually gentle, too, but sometimes the switch would come out.”
hunks.sol: “Yes, I remember. I had times like that, too. My Master was usually gentle, but sometimes he’d take out the switch.”

hunks.baseline: But the more he recalled those happy memories from long ago, the fainter the smile on the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s lips became.
hunks.sol: Yet the more he recalled those happy memories, the more the smile on his lips faded.

hunks.baseline: Once, all of that had been the present.
hunks.sol: Once, those days had been the present.

hunks.baseline: It had been today, and yesterday.
hunks.sol: They had been today, and yesterday.

hunks.baseline: But now, the only faces left in his memory were twisted hideously with pain. Only the sight of them dying, or already dead.
hunks.sol: But now, the only faces left in his memory were twisted hideously with pain. All he could see was them dead or dying.

hunks.baseline: *“You bastards! You’ll be cursed for this!”*
hunks.sol: *“You bastards! Heaven will punish you!”*

hunks.baseline: It was strange.
hunks.sol: It made no sense.

hunks.baseline: His mother’s piercing scream as the soldiers brutalized her while she fought to protect her only surviving child, and his Master’s final words—those memories were so vivid. So why were their smiling faces so faint?
hunks.sol: His mother’s piercing scream as soldiers brutalized her for resisting them to protect her only surviving child, and his Master’s final plea—those he remembered so clearly. Why, then, had their smiling faces grown so faint?

hunks.baseline: Why were they all blurred, as if hidden in fog?
hunks.sol: Why were they blurred as if lost in fog?

hunks.baseline: But, naturally, the pain that should have followed never came.
hunks.sol: But the pain that should have followed never came.

hunks.baseline: His lips, wet with blood, moved. His eyes, fixed on Jin Taekyung, the Bow Saint, and the countless people who had gathered around him, flickered with cold flames.
hunks.sol: His blood-wet lips moved. His eyes passed over Jin Taekyung, the Bow Saint, and the countless others who had gathered around him. Cold flames flickered in them.

hunks.baseline: He spat out the words.
Each syllable was filled with anger.
hunks.sol: He spat out each syllable, filling it with anger.

hunks.baseline: He swallowed his resentment toward the world—and his grief at knowing he could never be happy again.
hunks.sol: He swallowed his resentment toward the world and his grief at knowing he could never be happy again.

hunks.baseline: “Even if you’ve protected the imperial capital, you can’t stop the fires spreading throughout the land.”
hunks.sol: “Even if you’ve protected the Imperial Capital, you can’t stop the fires spreading throughout the land.”

hunks.baseline: He had served the imperial family for more than half a century. There wasn’t a single person who hadn’t taken shelter beneath his vast shadow, and not one of them was beyond Dark Heaven’s reach.
hunks.sol: He had spent more than half a century in the imperial court. No one had gone without sheltering for a time beneath his vast shadow, and no one had escaped Dark Heaven’s reach.

hunks.baseline: The frogs who had escaped the vast well of the imperial capital had each received an official post and spread throughout the land. They’d put down new roots, growing branches and bearing fruit.
hunks.sol: Those frogs had left the great well of the Imperial Capital, each taking up an official post somewhere in the land. There they had put down new roots, grown branches, and borne fruit.

hunks.baseline: Thinking of the Great Nation, soon to be swept up in a massive civil war and firestorm. Thinking of the Dark Heaven forces that would use those flames to march into the Central Plains.
hunks.sol: He thought of the Great Nation soon to be engulfed by civil war and a raging fire. He thought of Dark Heaven’s forces advancing into the Central Plains with those flames before them.

hunks.baseline: “That day, the Great Nation will fall.”
hunks.sol: “On that day, the Great Nation will fall.”

hunks.baseline: The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord threw his head back and laughed.
hunks.sol: The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord threw his head back and laughed, looking at the Emperor standing before him and mocking the helplessness he would feel.

hunks.baseline: He looked at the man standing before him, mocking the Emperor, who would feel helpless to do anything.
